tweets.text: 🇨🇳 Deadly fire tears through a Chinese shoe factory At least 28 people were reportedly killed when a fire tore through a shoe factory in Jinjiang, in China's Fujian province. It started on the ground floor around noon and shot up the building, feeding on all the flammable shoe materials inside, with workers trapped on the roof as black smoke swallowed the sky. Jinjiang is China's "shoe capital," thousands of factories cranking out a fifth of the world's shoes. Xi called the losses "significant" and ordered an all-out rescue. Source: CCTV, CNN, Reuters, TRT / Writer: Daniyal Video

tweets.text: 🇺🇸 When America chose the title of "president" for its leader, it was considered exceptionally unusual for a head of state. This clip from HBO's John Adams depicts that early debate. Adams favored a more royal-sounding title. Deriving from the Latin praesidere (meaning "to sit before"), president was historically reserved for ceremonial committee chairmen, university heads, or local club officers. It carried no connotations of supreme political or sovereign power. Today, we think nothing of it. At the time, pretty strange. Writer: Michael Video
